summary: Part 1 of Parkevtate Vosianc's Nike deep dive (the actual verdict sits in the members-only Part 2, so no call here). He lays out why the stock keeps making 52-week lows, down over 46% in 2026: management guided to a difficult fiscal year with pain possibly extending into next year; Q1 was in line but weakness concentrates in Sportswear, Jordan and Greater China; aged inventory is being cleared below cost, clogging wholesale partners' shelves and depressing future order books; and the cautious consumer is trading down as living costs outpace wages. He is openly skeptical of the Jordan scarcity strategy — deliberately cutting volume of the brand's best IP (retro pairs at $215) just as younger buyers' awareness of Michael Jordan fades — though he admits his earlier praise for Nike's DTC pivot proved wrong, so his skepticism may misfire again. Newness is the one bright spot where fresh products are landing. No explicit call in this video; stance recorded as UNCERTAIN pending Part 2.
